newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds seen holding levels in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds seen holding levels in quiet market.

text.p: Danish bond prices were virtually unchanged in a quiet market on Friday with dealers foreseeing a stable end to the week with current levels holding.
"We are experiencing a stable and calm market and that is the way things look like staying for the rest of the afternoon. I do not see bond prices losing ground, " one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down a marginal 0.03 point from the opening at 113.27, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark, due to take over on September 1, was unaltered at 105.95, The yields were 5.99 percent and 6.20 percent respectively.

Turnover for the 2006 benchmark was around 1.5 billion crowns, with the 2007 paper at one billion crowns. The 2006's September future rose 0.32 point to 112.56 with 25 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.05 point to 91.65. The crown traded at 3.8074 per mark at 1135 GMT, virtually the same as at the start of trading. The 2007 bond's 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 60 basis points.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling some 200 million crowns worth of the seven percent 2007 bond as part of its routine financing operations.
